title: My room
intro: Tom, the Australian student, shows you his small room in a Tehran flat. The whole story is in the first person ('I'), so it practises the -am verb endings (زندگی می‌کنم، دارم، می‌بینم), furniture words, 'there is' with هست and the ezafe that joins nouns and adjectives (یک فرش کوچک قرمز). His room has one visitor he did not expect.
source: An original story for this course.

sentences.fa: من یک اتاق کوچک در یک آپارتمان دارم.
sentences.r: man yek otāgh-e kuchak dar yek āpārtemān dāram.
sentences.en: I have a small room in a flat.

sentences.fa: در اتاق یک تخت، یک میز و یک صندلی هست.
sentences.r: dar otāgh yek takht, yek miz o yek sandali hast.
sentences.en: In the room there is a bed, a desk and a chair.

sentences.fa: روی میز کتاب‌های فارسی من هست.
sentences.r: ru-ye miz ketāb-hā-ye fārsi-ye man hast.
sentences.en: My Persian books are on the desk.

sentences.fa: یک فرش کوچک قرمز هم روی زمین است.
sentences.r: yek farsh-e kuchak-e ghermez ham ru-ye zamin ast.
sentences.en: There is also a small red rug on the floor.

sentences.fa: اتاق من یک پنجره‌ی بزرگ دارد.
sentences.r: otāgh-e man yek panjare-ye bozorg dārad.
sentences.en: My room has a big window.

sentences.fa: من از پنجره کوه‌های البرز را می‌بینم.
sentences.r: man az panjare kuh-hā-ye Alborz rā mi-binam.
sentences.en: From the window I can see the Alborz mountains.

sentences.fa: در زمستان، روی کوه‌ها برف هست.
sentences.r: dar zemestān, ru-ye kuh-hā barf hast.
sentences.en: In winter there is snow on the mountains.

sentences.fa: اتاق من کوچک است، اما من آن را خیلی دوست دارم.
sentences.r: otāgh-e man kuchak ast, ammā man ān rā kheyli dust dāram.
sentences.en: My room is small, but I like it very much.

sentences.fa: هر صبح، گربه‌ی همسایه از پنجره می‌آید و روی تخت من می‌خوابد!
sentences.r: har sobh, gorbe-ye hamsāye az panjare mi-āyad o ru-ye takht-e man mi-khābad!
sentences.en: Every morning the neighbour's cat comes in through the window and sleeps on my bed!

sentences.fa: حالا اتاق من یک گربه هم دارد!
sentences.r: hālā otāgh-e man yek gorbe ham dārad!
sentences.en: Now my room has a cat too!

options: in a big house in Shiraz
in a small room in a Tehran flat

questions.q: What can Tom see from his window?
Who sleeps on Tom's bed every morning?

after: Look at یک فرش کوچک قرمز 'a small red rug': the adjectives come after the noun, and each one is joined to the word before it by the ezafe -e (farsh-e kuchak-e ghermez), which is heard but not written. Persian says 'there is' in two ways: در اتاق یک تخت هست 'in the room there is a bed', and اتاق من یک پنجره دارد 'my room has a window'. And notice را in من آن را خیلی دوست دارم and کوه‌های البرز را می‌بینم: it marks a definite object, a thing we already know. The Alborz range rises straight up behind Tehran, and on clear winter days the snowy peaks are visible from all over the city.
